steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Deposit the US$250 minimum by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Adjust the risk controls, pick a mode and practise on the demo before going live.

pros: Fast setup - minutes to a live dashboard.
Free registration and a demo account.
cons: No independent audit of the models.
Registration details not stated up front.
The demo claim buried in the signup flow.
redFlags: Restriction lists that name different countries.
Payout promises with no processing detail.
No regulator, licence or audit named anywhere.

faqs.a: Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.
11 crypto assets through broker partners, per the published pages. The list varies between sections, so check the dashboard after signup.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$250 minimum.
The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.

bottomLine: The desk, the demo and the funding options all check out. The score reflects the paperwork around them.
We rate it 4.6 with conditions: the platform is usable, the published claims are not all verifiable, and the US$250 minimum is the right size for testing either.
